subject: Admin-event ledger: WORM archive policy, export window, and legal-hold interaction
messages:
From: Claire Bishop <claire.bishop@crestassurance.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request for admin-event ledger WORM archive policy and export window

Hi Kimberly,

We're working through Crest's SIG assessment and need to document how Redwood treats admin-event logs for attestation purposes. A few specific asks we hope you can clarify (bullet answers are fine):

- What admin events are recorded (user sign-ins, role changes, API key operations, privileged session starts, console actions, etc.)? Please call out anything that is NOT currently captured.
- Does Redwood offer a WORM (Write Once Read Many) archive option for admin-event snapshots? If so, how is immutability implemented (storage backend, retention enforcement, tamper-evidence)?
- For exports: what are the standard export windows (on-demand snapshot, daily/weekly scheduled snapshots, streaming CDC)? How long does it take to produce an attested snapshot placed in a customer-provided S3?
- How do legal holds interact with retention/WORM? Can a hold extend retention beyond configured retention windows and are holds reversible?
- Do exports include a signed manifest/HMAC for integrity verification? If so, what algorithm and key management is used?

If you already have a short spec or slide we can attach to the SIG, that would be perfect. Thanks — Claire

--
Claire Bishop
Senior Assurance Manager, Crest Assurance
claire.bishop@crestassurance.com
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Claire Bishop <claire.bishop@crestassurance.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for admin-event ledger WORM archive policy and export window

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below; I attached a short spec (admin_export_spec_v2.pdf) with examples and expected timelines. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if useful.

What we log (high level):
- Auth events: successful/failed sign-ins, 2FA actions, SSO assertions (provider, issuer), session durations.
- Privileged actions: role/grant changes, admin console operations (create/delete user, change permissions), API key creation/deactivation.
- Operator/infra events: host/service restarts relevant to admin tooling, scaling actions triggered by operators.
- KV cache / model access events: operator-triggered model loading/unloading and cache flush actions (included where they affect admin state).
- NOTE: We do NOT currently log full command-line arguments from ephemeral infra hosts by default; we can enable additional operator-level detail under a customer request.

WORM / immutability:
- We offer an optional WORM snapshot pipeline for admin-event snapshots. Implementation: generated snapshot files are written to an immutable storage tier (S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode) in a holding bucket we control, then copied (read-only) to a customer-provided S3 if requested. Immutability is enforced via object locks + access controls and signed manifests.
- Tamper-evidence: each snapshot includes a signed manifest (SHA-256 checksums + timestamp) and an enveloped signature using an HSM-backed key. We also provide an attestation document signed by Redwood security.

Export windows & timelines:
- On-demand snapshot: available within 4–8 hours for small tenants (<=30M events), up to 24–48 hours for very large tenants (we'll size and confirm).
- Scheduled: daily/weekly snapshots available (configurable).
- Streaming/CDC: we offer a near-real-time export stream for operational telemetry (not the canonical snapshot; streaming has different retention/immutability semantics).

Legal hold interaction:
- Legal holds can be placed at the tenant level; when applied, we move affected objects into a hold state that prevents deletion even if retention policy would have expired. Holds are reversible only by the holder (with audit trail) and require an explicit release operation.
- Placing a hold does NOT remove WORM protections — it extends the effective retention by preventing deletion until release.

Integrity & key management:
- Signed manifests use SHA-256 checksums + RSA-PSS signatures. Signing keys are stored in our KMS/HSM. We can support customer-managed KMS for enterprise Private deployments (bring-your-own-key).

Next steps:
- I've attached admin_export_spec_v2.pdf with concrete S3 paths, required IAM role, sample manifest, and a runbook for attestation delivery.
- If Crest needs Redwood-signed attestations (DocuSign), we can produce a short attestation template; Aditya, can your team prepare a draft attestation for legal review? Jordan — can you estimate lead time for a large (>=500M event) on-demand export?

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Claire Bishop <claire.bishop@crestassurance.com>

Subject: Re: Request for admin-event ledger WORM archive policy and export window

Hi Kimberly — this is helpful, thanks. Two quick clarifications:

1) For the signed manifest: will the manifest include per-file byte ranges and checksums (we need to be able to prove partial-file integrity if slices are delivered)? Also, can we expect the manifest to contain a Redwood signature + key id?
2) For legal holds: is there any audit trail proving who placed/removed a hold (timestamp + actor)? We typically require a non-repudiable trail.

If you can include a sample signed manifest in the spec (even as a stub) that would be perfect. We'll plan a short call only if needed after we review the PDF.

Thanks — Claire

Folks — forwarding Crest's follow-up. This thread will be part of a SIG/CAIQ package; we need two deliverables: a short signed attestation and a sample signed manifest (stub acceptable for the packet). Attachments: draft-attestation.txt (for legal to review), export-playbook.md (runbook for on-demand exports and manifest generation).

Action items:
- Aditya: please draft the attestation wording (one-paragraph statement of process + signature block) and attach DocuSign metadata (DOCUSIGN-REQ-4372). Legal will likely request small edits; aim to have a first draft by EOD Friday.
- Jordan: estimate lead times for large on-demand exports and confirm the operational steps/time-to-complete for 100M / 500M / 1B event buckets. Also confirm whether streaming exports can be HMAC-signed in-flight or if we must only rely on snapshot manifests for tamper-evidence.
- I'll prepare the sample manifest stub (include file-level checksums, byte ranges, signing key id) and a short appendix describing the S3 Object Lock configuration.

Please keep this internal until we have the draft attestation and manifest.

Thanks — Kim
